synopsis: A man tries to wash his hands only to find that his bar of soap behaves exactly like solid glass, cracking into sharp shards.
narration: Washing my hands before dinner and this bar just cracked like a window. It feels like real glass now. Is this even safe to touch?

shots.prompt: A rectangular bar of light pink soap with a faint brand imprint on top and one bright glassy break face along its long edge. glass-hard soap with sharp conchoidal fracture edges and glossy translucent shards catching hard specular light. The frame remains completely locked from a straight-on eye-level angle looking down into the sink basin. An ordinary home bathroom counter: graphite-grey stone top around a white ceramic basin with a faint water ring, matte tiles behind, and cool daylight from a small frosted window blended with warm mirror light. Hands wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt hold the pink bar of soap under a running faucet, the bar filling most of the frame. The bar is already split along a bright conchoidal fracture; its glassy translucent edge throws hard specular glints under the water while the broken face holds a mirror-smooth shine and water beads roll off the sharp facets.
shots.violation_observation: the soaked bar keeps a bright glassy fracture face with sharp translucent edges
shots.state_carry: a bright conchoidal fracture face on the pink bar
